name: Granulomatous Slack Skin

criteria.description: Presence of pendulous, lax, and wrinkled skin plaques typically in flexural areas
Skin biopsy showing granulomatous infiltrate with multinucleated giant cells and elastophagocytosis
Detection of atypical T-cell infiltrate consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
Chronic indolent progression with possible association to mycosis fungoides

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical skin lesions plus confirmatory histopathology and immunophenotyping findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, histological, and immunophenotypic features; no standardized criteria exist.

laboratory: Skin biopsy with granulomatous infiltrate and elastophagocytosis
Immunohistochemistry showing atypical CD4+ T-cell infiltrate
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing regional lymphadenopathy
Rarely PET-CT for staging of associated lymphoma
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; T-cell receptor gene rearrangement may be detected
other: Clinical correlation with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma spectrum

distinguishingFeatures: More widespread patch and plaque distribution without pendulous skin laxity
Typically presents with annular papules and plaques without skin laxity
Histology lacks elastophagocytosis and atypical T-cell infiltrate

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin laxity and plaque size
Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Ulceration or secondary infection of skin lesions
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
